definitions.gloss: mutual understanding; communication; getting on the same page
definitions.explanation: The process of conveying one's intentions and understanding another's, resulting in shared comprehension. Emphasizes the two-way nature of communication and whether both parties truly understand each other.

examples.japanese: {意思疎通|いしそつう}を{図|はか}る。
{言葉|ことば}の{壁|かべ}で{意思疎通|いしそつう}が{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Communication is difficult due to the language barrier.

examples.japanese: チーム{内|ない}の{意思疎通|いしそつう}が{不足|ふそく}していたことがミスの{原因|げんいん}だった。
examples.english: Insufficient communication within the team was the cause of the mistake.

notes: Composed of {意思|いし} (intention, will) + {疎通|そつう} (mutual understanding, free flow). The most common collocation is {意思疎通|いしそつう}を{図|はか}る (to seek/attempt mutual understanding). Also: {意思疎通|いしそつう}が{取|と}れる (to be able to communicate), {意思疎通|いしそつう}が{不足|ふそく}している (there is a lack of communication). A formal, slightly stiff word often used in business and organizational contexts. More casual alternatives: コミュニケーション, {話|はな}し{合|あ}い (discussion).
